<!-- generated by scripts/gen-reference.mjs; do not edit -->

The public include files in `Assets/Omni/Runtime/Sharders`. Ordinary URP shaders and Shader Graphs are converted when you switch to logarithmic rendering, so you do not need to include anything yourself ([Shader Graph and custom shaders](../../../docs/guides/shader-graph/)). Only when you hand-write a shader that supports Radial directly, use them as follows:

| Purpose | Include |
| --- | --- |
| Passes of a hand-written URP shader other than MotionVectors | `RadialVertexInject.hlsl` |
| MotionVectors and XRMotionVectors passes of a hand-written URP shader | `RadialObjectMotionVectors.hlsl` after `RadialVertexInject.hlsl` |
| Shader Graph | The converter adds Custom Functions from `RadialWarpNode.hlsl`. Do not include it by hand |

```hlsl
#include "Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.universal/Shaders/LitInput.hlsl"
#define OMNI_RADIAL_EXPECT_ACTIVE 1
#include "Assets/Omni/Runtime/Sharders/RadialVertexInject.hlsl"
// include the pass implementation after this
```

For Omni to treat the shader as Radial-capable, it must declare `_RadialGlobal_UseRadialTransform` in its Properties ([Global properties and defines](../globals/)). The bundled Radial shaders (for example `Assets/Omni/Radial/Universal Render Pipeline/Shaders/Lit.shader`) are working examples of the Properties declarations and the include order.

## RadialWarpNode.hlsl

`Assets/Omni/Runtime/Sharders/RadialWarpNode.hlsl`

The entry point for Shader Graph Custom Functions. The Custom Function nodes that the converter adds to a graph use the functions in this file ([Custom Function](../custom-functions/)). It includes `RadialInject.hlsl` and `RadialVertexHooks.hlsl` and connects the graph's vertices to the Radial projection. Graph includes are expanded into every pass, so it disables the vertex hooks automatically in the ShadowCaster, Meta, Decal Projector and Fullscreen passes. In passes that write depth (color, DepthOnly, DepthNormals) it adds per-pixel depth, and in graphs that use the depth texture it replaces Scene Depth and `SampleSceneDepth` with versions that return physical depth. Do not include it from hand-written shaders.

## RadialVertexInject.hlsl

`Assets/Omni/Runtime/Sharders/RadialVertexInject.hlsl`

The vertex entry point for hand-written and generated URP shaders. It includes `RadialInject.hlsl` and then `RadialVertexHooks.hlsl`. Include it after `Core.hlsl` and the material inputs (such as `LitInput.hlsl`), and before each pass implementation. In the ShadowCaster and Meta passes it defines `OMNI_RADIAL_HOOKS_DISABLED` to disable the vertex hooks (those passes render in physical space). If `OMNI_RADIAL_EXPECT_ACTIVE` is defined beforehand, including it before `Core.hlsl` is a compile error.

## RadialInject.hlsl

`Assets/Omni/Runtime/Sharders/RadialInject.hlsl`

The shared Radial implementation. It includes `RadialWarp.hlsl` and holds the camera packet (`_OmniRadialCamera_*`), the per-material `_RadialGlobal_*` declarations, and the functions that transform from object space to camera-relative mapped positions and reconstruct depth. On its own it does not replace any URP functions. `_RadialGlobal_*` is declared in the `RadialGlobalPerMaterial` CBUFFER (the Shader Graph, DOTS Instancing and Scene BRG paths each use their own declarations).

## RadialVertexHooks.hlsl

`Assets/Omni/Runtime/Sharders/RadialVertexHooks.hlsl`

Hooks that connect URP's vertex entry points from object space to the camera-relative mapped clip space. It replaces `GetVertexPositionInputs`, `GetVertexNormalInputs`, `TransformObjectToHClip`, `TransformObjectToWorldNormal`, `TransformObjectToWorldDir`, `GetWorldSpaceNormalizeViewDir` and `GetWorldSpaceViewDir` with macros, so it must come before the pass implementation that uses them. Do not include it on its own: without `RadialInject.hlsl` before it, compilation fails. When URP's `Core.hlsl` is missing or `OMNI_RADIAL_HOOKS_DISABLED` is defined, it replaces nothing. Normally it is included through `RadialVertexInject.hlsl`.

## RadialObjectMotionVectors.hlsl

`Assets/Omni/Runtime/Sharders/RadialObjectMotionVectors.hlsl`

A complete MotionVectors pass implementation that builds motion vectors from the current and previous object positions. It contains `#pragma vertex vert` and `#pragma fragment frag` and defines `vert` and `frag`. In the MotionVectors and XRMotionVectors passes, include it with `#include_with_pragmas` after `RadialVertexInject.hlsl`, in place of URP's `ObjectMotionVectors.hlsl`. With `_ALPHATEST_ON` it uses `_BaseMap`, `_BaseColor` and `_Cutoff`, so the material input declarations are required. On the first frame, after switching from non-Radial, and for rigid anchors, it outputs zero velocity instead of fake motion. Do not use it for ordinary Forward passes.

## RadialWarp.hlsl

`Assets/Omni/Runtime/Sharders/RadialWarp.hlsl`

The file that holds only the Radial mapping math. There is a single mapping, Smooth Log: `F(d) = S·log2(1 + d·M/S)` with S = 1. Inputs and outputs are always vectors relative to the Logical warp center; it never handles absolute world coordinates, the camera position or Unity's view matrix. It defines `OMNI_RADIAL_MODE_SMOOTHLOG` and `OMNI_RADIAL_MODE_IDENTITY`. `RadialInject.hlsl` includes it, so you normally do not include it directly. The `S` and reserved parameters of its functions are kept only to preserve the callers' signatures and are not read.
